blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
An audit is an independent check. It looks at the company's accounts to see if they are honest and follow the rules. External auditors come from outside the company. Usually they come once a year. They check the books carefully and give an opinion.

Internal controls are the small rules a company uses every day. They help to prevent mistakes and fraud. For example: two signatures for big payments, regular reconciliations, separation of duties, password protection, and audit trails.

Together, audits and internal controls keep the company honest. This is not because the company does not trust its people. Good systems protect everyone — including the people who want to do the right thing.

items.q: How often do external auditors usually come?
items.why: "External auditors come from outside the company. Usually they come once a year."

items.q: Where do external auditors come from?
items.why: "External auditors come from outside the company." Por isso o check é independente.

items.q: What do internal controls help to prevent?
items.why: "They help to prevent mistakes and fraud."

items.q: The text suggests that good systems…
items.why: Inferência: "Good systems protect everyone — including the people who want to do the right thing."

items.q: Which idea would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Two signatures can be used for big payments
An audit is an independent check
Internal controls are used every day
Controls exist because the company does not trust its people
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que os controles NÃO existem por desconfiança, mas para proteger todos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicar a regra das duas assinaturas para um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team! Let me explain one rule quickly. For big payments, we always need two signatures. One person cannot send a large amount of money alone. I sign, and then a second person signs too.

Some new people think this rule means we do not trust them. That is not true. The rule is here to protect you. If only one signature is needed and something goes wrong, everyone will look at you. With two signatures, two people check the payment together.

We also do a reconciliation every week. We compare our numbers with the bank numbers. If there is a small mistake, we find it early, before it becomes a big problem.

And every action leaves an audit trail. So later, if someone asks a question, we can show exactly what happened and when. The system remembers for us.

Here at Czarnikow, these controls are not a punishment. They protect the company, and they protect you too. Good systems are quiet when they work well. You only notice them when they are missing. It is simple, it is safe, and it keeps all of us honest. Any questions? Good — let's start.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many signatures are needed for big payments?
items.why: "For big payments, we always need two signatures."

items.q: How often does the team do a reconciliation?
items.why: "We also do a reconciliation every week."

items.q: According to Charlotte, why is the two-signature rule good for the new person?
options: It means they can work alone
It protects them if something goes wrong
items.why: "The rule is here to protect you… two people check the payment together."

items.q: Charlotte suggests that the audit trail is useful because…
options: it shows later what happened and when
items.why: Inferência: "we can show exactly what happened and when" — a trilha guarda o registro para depois.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's message to the new colleague?
options: The rules are there to protect everyone
The rules are only for managers
items.why: Inferência: ela deixa claro que a regra não é desconfiança, e sim proteção para todos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The company had an audit last month." An audit is…
options: an independent check of the accounts
items.why: Audit = auditoria: uma verificação independente das contas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "These small daily rules are our ___ controls."
items.why: Internal control = controle interno: as regras diárias da própria empresa.

items.q: "The auditors are independent." Independent means…
items.why: Independent = independente: não é controlado pela empresa que está sendo checada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We want to ___ mistakes before they happen."
items.why: To prevent = prevenir: parar algo antes de acontecer.

items.q: "We do a reconciliation every week." A reconciliation is…
options: comparing two sets of numbers to find mistakes
items.why: Reconciliation = conciliação: comparar números (por exemplo, os da empresa e os do banco).

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando falamos de auditoria e controles. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the big payment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new control in every office." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = implementar, colocar em uso aos poucos.

items.q: "Please keep an eye on the weekly numbers." This means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, observar com atenção.

items.q: "The auditor asked us to follow through on the plan." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "If we cut corners, the audit will find a problem." To cut corners means to…
options: skip important steps to save time
items.why: Cut corners = pular etapas importantes para economizar tempo (e criar risco).
